classification.difficultyReason: Connect two isosceles triangles, tangent perpendicularity and an exterior angle in a; in b turn equal radii and the supplied equal segment into a sine ratio, then recover the angle.

spec.description: Tangent TA; O,B,A collinear. Double ticks TB=BA; alpha at A and beta=OBT. No derived right angles or conclusions supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied givens and targets only; no derived numerical values or proof conclusions.

answer.worked: Since TB=BA, $\angle BTA=\alpha$. Since OB=OT, $\angle BTO=\beta$. Radius OT is perpendicular to tangent TA, so $\alpha+\beta=90^\circ$. As O,B,A are collinear, the exterior-angle theorem in triangle ABT gives $\beta=2\alpha$. Thus $3\alpha=90^\circ$, so $\alpha=30^\circ$.

spec.description: Tangent TA; O,B,A collinear. Double ticks OB=BA; alpha at A and beta=OBT. No derived right angles or conclusions supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied givens and targets only; no derived numerical values or proof conclusions.

answer.worked: OT=OB (radii), and OB=BA (given), so OA=2OT. Since radius OT is perpendicular to tangent TA, triangle OTA is right-angled at T. Hence $\sin\alpha=\frac{OT}{OA}=\frac{OT}{(2OT)}=\tfrac12$.

The acute angle $\alpha$ has $\sin\alpha=\tfrac12$, so $\alpha=30^\circ$. In right triangle OTA, $\angle TOA=60^\circ$. Since O,B,A are collinear, $\angle TOB=60^\circ$. Also OT=OB (radii), so the base angles of triangle OTB are equal and each is $\frac{(180^\circ-60^\circ)}{2}=60^\circ$. Hence $\beta=60^\circ$.
